title: Password Reset and SSO Login Guide
sections: This article explains how users regain access when they forget a password or when single sign-on stops working on this edition. It covers members, guests and workspace owners. Self-service reset starts from the Forgot password link on the sign-in page, which sends a one-time link to the email address on the account. The link expires after {reset_link_ttl} minutes and works only once; requesting a new link cancels every earlier one. If no message arrives within five minutes, ask the user to check quarantine and spam folders before raising a ticket. Agents must never ask for a current password, a full recovery code or a screenshot of the authenticator app, and any message requesting one should be reported to the security mailbox as phishing.

A new password must be at least {password_min_length} characters long and cannot match any of the previous ten passwords on the account. Passphrases are accepted and encouraged; there is no requirement for symbols, but every new password is checked against a list of known breached passwords and rejected if it appears there. After {lockout_attempts} consecutive failed sign-in attempts the account is locked for {lockout_minutes} minutes. The lock clears on its own, and a successful password reset also clears it immediately. Agents can see the lock status and the time it ends on the user record, but they cannot unlock an account manually, because doing so would bypass the protection against password guessing.

When a workspace uses single sign-on, users authenticate through {sso_protocol}. If the administrator has set SSO to enforced, the Forgot password link is hidden for managed users and passwords must be reset in the company identity provider, not in the product. Agents should not try to send a product reset link in this case, because it will be ignored. Administrators configure the connection under {sso_settings_path}, where they upload the identity provider metadata, map the email attribute and choose which domains are managed. Unmanaged users, such as external guests, keep their own password and use the normal reset flow even when SSO is enforced for everyone else in the workspace.

Most SSO failures come from configuration drift on the identity provider side. The three common errors are an expired signing certificate, an email attribute that no longer matches the address in the workspace, and clock drift between servers larger than the tolerated window of three minutes. Ask the administrator to download the SSO debug log from the connection page and attach it to the ticket. A successful SSO sign-in creates a session that lasts {session_hours} hours, after which users are sent back to the identity provider to authenticate again. Signing out of the identity provider does not end an active product session; administrators who need that should revoke sessions from the user record.

If self-service steps do not restore access, open a ticket in the Access queue with the workspace ID, the affected email domain and the exact error text. The first response target for this edition is {response_target}. When the person locked out is the only workspace owner, recovery requires identity verification before any change is made. That check is run by {person} ({email}) on the identity assurance team, who can be reached on {phone} for urgent cases during business hours. Verification usually takes one business day once the documents arrive. Agents must not transfer ownership, change the account email or disable SSO on request without a completed verification record.

variants.label: Lumora Cloud, Government region

slots.sso_protocol: SAML 2.0 with signed assertions and smart card step-up

variants.extra_section: Government region addendum: sign-in for this region is accepted only from network ranges registered by the customer, and reset links are blocked when they are requested from an unregistered address. Every reset, lockout and SSO configuration change is written to an audit log that the customer can export for {audit_retention_years} years. Support staff handling these tickets must hold the regional clearance and work from the dedicated support environment, never from a personal device or a shared office machine.

variants.label: Lumora Server 7.2, self-hosted
variants.extra_section: Version 7.2 addendum: this release reaches end of support on {eol_date}. Its LDAP connector caches group membership for one hour, so a user removed from the directory can still sign in until the cache refreshes. Administrators can force a refresh from the command line with the directory sync tool. Customers should plan the upgrade to 8.0, which replaces the cache with live directory lookups and removes this delay.

title: Remote Access VPN Setup
sections: This guide covers installing and connecting the corporate remote access VPN for the group named in the title. The supported client is {client_version}, distributed through the company software center; copies downloaded from other sources are blocked by the gateway. Before installing, the device must be enrolled in device management and show a compliant status, otherwise the client installs but the connection is refused at the posture check. Installation needs no admin rights on managed devices. After installation, sign out and back in once so the client service starts with the user session. The client checks for updates every day and installs them silently at the next disconnect.

The client connects to {gateway_host}, which is preloaded in the connection profile and should never be edited by hand. Authentication uses {auth_method}. The device certificate is issued automatically during enrollment and renewed every twelve months; an expired certificate shows as error 809 or as a failed TLS handshake in the client log. Users who replace their phone must register the new authenticator before the old one is wiped, or they will need an identity check at the service desk to reset their second factor. Shared or kiosk devices cannot connect at all, because the certificate is bound to a named user.

Routing policy for this group: {split_tunnel_policy}. Users should not install a second VPN product, a personal proxy or a browser privacy extension that tunnels traffic, as these conflict with the routing table and break name resolution for internal hosts. Internal sites are reached by their short names only while connected; if a short name does not resolve, run the repair DNS action in the client before opening a ticket. Printing to office printers from home is not supported through the VPN. Large file transfers to internal shares are allowed but should use the sync client rather than a mapped drive for reliability.

Common connection problems have known fixes. If pages load partially or uploads hang, the network path is probably dropping large packets; set the client MTU to {mtu_value} under advanced settings and reconnect. If the client connects and then drops after a few minutes on hotel or airport networks, switch the transport from UDP to TCP. Sessions are disconnected after {idle_timeout} without traffic, and the client then asks for the second factor again. Collect logs with the export diagnostics button, which bundles the client log, the routing table and the posture check result into one archive that can be attached to the ticket.

The IT service desk supports this group from {helpdesk_hours}. Outside those hours, only full gateway outages are handled, through the on-call line. For an individual connection problem, open a ticket in the Network Access category with the diagnostics archive, the network type (home, mobile hotspot or public) and the time of the last failure. Repeated certificate or posture failures on the same device are escalated to the endpoint team. Regional VPN questions and access requests for restricted subnets go to {person} ({email}), the network access owner for this group, who approves or rejects them within two business days.

Extensions must be requested by the sponsoring manager at least {extension_notice_days} working days in advance. Contractors may only connect from devices issued or approved by the company, never from a personal machine, and their sessions are recorded.

title: Customer Refund Policy
sections: This policy tells agents when a customer can get their money back for an order placed with the store named in the title and how to process it. Customers may return most items within {refund_window} of delivery for a full refund of the item price. The window starts on the delivery date recorded by the carrier, not the order date. Orders delivered in several parcels have one window per parcel. Items bought as gifts can be returned by the recipient with the gift receipt, in which case the refund goes to the original payment method and the buyer is told by email. Personalised items, opened hygiene products and gift cards are never refundable.

Returned items must arrive complete, with accessories and manuals. Unopened items are refunded in full. Opened items that work and show no damage are refunded minus a restocking fee of {restocking_fee}, which covers inspection and repackaging. Damaged or incomplete returns are either sent back to the customer at our cost or refunded at a reduced amount agreed with them in writing. Agents may waive the restocking fee once per customer per year when the customer has a good order history, and must record the waiver reason on the order. Items marked final sale on the product page follow a special rule: {sale_items_rule}.

{return_shipping_rule} When an item arrives faulty or the wrong item was sent, return shipping is always free and the original delivery charge is refunded too. Customers should use the prepaid label generated from their order page; returns sent without a label, or with a different carrier, are accepted but may take longer to match to the order. Collection from the customer's address is available for items above thirty kilograms, and the agent books it directly in the carrier portal. Never ask a customer to pay a carrier directly or to send cash, and never accept a return at an office.

Refunds are issued once the warehouse confirms the return, usually within two working days of receipt. The money then reaches the customer within {processing_days}, depending on the bank. {refund_method_rule} Customers who paid with a gift card receive store credit, which never expires. If a customer reports that a refund has not arrived after the stated time, check the refund reference in the payment console and send it to them so their bank can trace it, before opening an investigation with the payments team. Do not issue a second refund while the first one is still pending.

Agents can approve refunds up to {approval_threshold} on their own. Larger refunds, refunds outside the return window and any refund to a different payment method than the one used for the order need approval from a team lead. The current approver for this region is {person} ({email}). Goodwill refunds without a return, such as for a late delivery or a minor defect the customer chooses to keep, are capped at twenty percent of the item price and are tracked monthly per agent. Suspected abuse, for example repeated returns of used items, should be flagged to the fraud team instead of being refused in the chat.

title: Billing Disputes and Chargebacks
sections: This article explains how support handles a customer who disagrees with a charge, and what happens when a customer goes straight to their bank instead. A billing dispute is a request to support to correct an invoice. Customers can raise one within {dispute_window} of the invoice date, through the billing page or by replying to the invoice email. Agents should first check the usage records and the plan history, because most disputes come from seats added by another admin, a proration after a plan change, or tax applied after a missing VAT number. Explain the charge line by line before offering any credit.

Agents may issue a service credit of up to {agent_credit_limit} per account per billing period without approval, for example when a charge is correct but the customer was confused by a plan change. Credits are applied to the next invoice and never paid out as cash. Corrections larger than that, or any refund of a paid invoice, go to the {finance_queue} queue with the invoice number, the disputed amount and a short explanation. Finance answers within three business days. While a dispute is open the disputed amount is excluded from dunning emails, but the rest of the invoice remains due on the normal date.

A chargeback happens when the customer asks their bank or card issuer to reverse the payment. The payment provider notifies us and debits the amount immediately, plus a non-refundable fee of {chargeback_fee}. We have {chargeback_response_days} to submit evidence, so chargeback tickets are always set to high priority. Evidence normally includes the signed order form or the accepted terms, sign-in logs showing the service was used, the invoice and any messages where the customer acknowledged the charge. The payments team assembles and submits the evidence; support agents only collect the conversation history and must never pressure the customer to withdraw the claim.

While a chargeback is open, {suspension_rule} If the customer wins, the debit stands and the account balance shows the reversed amount as unpaid. If we win, the funds return to us within about two weeks. Customers who want to settle can pay the amount by bank transfer to the collections account {iban}, quoting the invoice number, after which we tell the bank that the dispute is resolved. A second chargeback on the same account within twelve months leads to a mandatory switch to invoice billing with payment in advance, and the customer is told this in writing.

Unpaid amounts that cannot be recovered are written off by finance. Support can recommend a write-off for small balances up to {writeoff_limit}, for example the remainder of a disputed proration, but cannot approve it. Above that amount the decision belongs to the credit controller, currently {person} ({email}), who reviews cases weekly. Never promise a customer that a balance will be cancelled before the write-off is approved and visible on the account. Record every dispute outcome in the billing history tab, as the information is used in annual revenue audits and in any later legal claim.

slots.suspension_rule: the account stays active, but no new seats or add-ons can be bought.

Disputes from government buyers paying with a purchasing card go to the public sector billing desk, not to the standard queue, because those buyers follow their own dispute procedure. Log each copy request on the ticket with the date it was sent and the method used.

Only debits disputed as unauthorised follow the chargeback steps above. Customers who change bank must sign a new mandate, because the old mandate reference cannot be reused with a different account. If the retry also fails, the customer is asked to pay the open invoice by card within seven days.

title: API Rate Limits and Throttling
sections: Every request to the Orbitly API counts against the limits of the workspace that owns the API key, not the individual key, so splitting traffic over several keys does not raise the ceiling. On this tier the sustained limit is {requests_per_minute} requests per minute, measured over a rolling sixty second window. Short spikes are absorbed by a burst allowance of {burst_allowance} requests, which refills at the sustained rate. Read and write calls share the same budget. Health checks and the token endpoint are exempt. Limits apply per region, so a workspace using two regions has two separate budgets.

Besides the per minute limit, the API caps the number of requests in flight at the same time at {concurrency_limit} per workspace. Requests above that number are rejected at once rather than queued. Long running calls such as report generation hold a slot until they finish, so integrations that start many reports in parallel are the usual cause of concurrency errors. There is also a daily quota of {daily_quota} requests, reset at midnight UTC. Usage against both limits is visible in the developer dashboard with a one minute delay, and an email warning is sent when the daily quota reaches eighty percent.

Bulk endpoints accept many records per call and are the recommended way to import or sync large datasets. On this tier a bulk call can carry up to {bulk_batch_size} records and counts as a single request against the per minute limit, but each record counts against the daily quota. Bulk jobs run asynchronously: the call returns a job ID, and the client should poll the job status endpoint no more than once every ten seconds. Polling faster than that is itself throttled. Failed records are listed in the job result and can be resubmitted without resending the whole batch.

When a limit is exceeded the API returns HTTP status 429 with a JSON error body naming the limit that was hit. {retry_guidance} Clients should back off exponentially with jitter, starting at one second and capping at sixty seconds, and must not retry immediately in a tight loop. Repeated violations over an hour can trigger a temporary block of fifteen minutes on the workspace, which shows as status 403 with the reason code rate_block. The official SDKs already implement this back-off, so customers seeing frequent blocks are usually calling the API with their own HTTP client.

Customers who need higher limits should first check whether bulk endpoints and caching cover their case. {limit_increase_rule} Requests are reviewed by the platform team, who look at the last thirty days of traffic before deciding. Temporary increases for a migration or a launch are possible for up to two weeks. For contractual questions, the customer's account manager is {person} ({email}). Support agents must not promise a specific limit before the platform team has approved it, and any approved change is recorded on the workspace so other agents can see it.

title: Exporting Your Account Data
sections: This article explains how customers can get a copy of their data out of the product, either for their own records, for an auditor or before moving to another system. Exports are started from Settings, Data, Export, and only users with the {export_role} role can see that page. Each export is a snapshot of the data at the moment the job starts; later changes are not included. The customer chooses a date range and the record types, such as ledgers, invoices, contacts or payroll runs. Exports include custom fields but not saved report layouts or dashboard settings, which must be recreated by hand in the new system.

Data is exported as {export_formats}. Each file holds at most {max_rows} rows; larger record sets are split into numbered files inside one archive, and the archive includes a manifest listing the row count per file so customers can check that nothing is missing. Amounts are exported in the account's base currency with a separate column for the transaction currency. Dates use the ISO format regardless of the language setting. Customers importing into a spreadsheet should open the files with UTF-8 encoding, otherwise names with accents appear garbled, which is the most common export complaint we receive.

Document attachments such as receipts and scanned invoices are handled separately: {attachments_rule} Attachments keep their original file names, prefixed with the record ID so they can be matched back. Large attachment exports can take several hours. The customer receives an email when the archive is ready, with a download link that stays valid for {link_expiry_hours} hours and works only for the user who started the export. If the link expires the export can be started again; there is no limit on the number of manual exports per day, but only one can run at a time.

{scheduled_exports} Scheduled and manual exports appear in the export history, which shows who started each job, when and with which filters. The history is kept for one year and is often requested by auditors. If an export fails, the history shows the error code: E-TIMEOUT usually means the date range is too wide and should be split, while E-PERM means the user lost the required role while the job was running. Agents can rerun a failed export on the customer's behalf only after the customer confirms the filters in writing, and they note the confirmation on the ticket.

When a subscription is cancelled the account becomes read-only, and exports remain available for {retention_after_cancel}. After that period the data is deleted and cannot be exported, even if the customer reactivates. Customers who need an export after this point, for a tax inspection for example, should be told plainly that it is no longer possible. Requests for exports in a custom format or a direct database extract are not part of the standard service; forward them to the data services lead, {person} ({email}), who can quote for professional services work and agree a delivery date with the customer.

title: Account Deletion and Data Erasure Requests
sections: This article describes what happens when a customer asks to close their account and have their data erased, and what support must check before starting. Only the account owner can request deletion, through Settings, Account, Delete account, or in writing to support from the owner's email address. {confirmation_method} Before deletion, remind the customer that it is permanent and suggest they export their data first, as described in the data export article. Accounts with an unpaid balance can still be deleted, but the balance remains due and is handled by collections. Deletion of a single user inside an account is a different process and is done by the account admin.

After the request is confirmed, the account enters a grace period of {grace_period_days} days. During that time users cannot sign in, scheduled jobs and integrations stop, and the owner can cancel the deletion by replying to the confirmation email or by asking support. When the grace period ends, the account and its data are permanently removed from the live systems within {purge_days} days. The customer receives a final email when this is done. Support cannot restore any data after that point, and reactivating with the same email address creates a new, empty account with no history.

Backups are not edited record by record. Deleted data remains in encrypted backups until those backups expire, which happens {backup_purge_days} days after the live deletion. Backups are only used to recover from a platform incident, and if a restore ever happens, previously deleted accounts are deleted again before the system goes back online. Customers sometimes ask for a certificate of deletion; we can provide a standard letter confirming the dates of live deletion and backup expiry, signed by the data protection team, but not a log of each individual record.

Some records must be kept by law even after the account is deleted. For this region we keep {retained_records} for {retention_years} years, in a restricted archive that only the finance and legal teams can access. These records are not used for marketing or analytics. The rest of the account data, including users, contacts, documents and attachments, is deleted as described above. If a customer objects to the retention, explain the legal basis and offer to forward the objection to the data protection officer rather than arguing the point in the ticket.

Requests made under data protection law, such as a right to erasure request from an individual user rather than the account owner, must be answered within {response_deadline}. Log them in the privacy queue the same day, even if they arrive through chat or social media. The data protection officer for this region is {person} ({email}), and postal requests can be sent to {address}. Never ask the requester why they want their data erased, and do not require them to use a specific form. Identity checks are allowed only to the extent needed to confirm that the request comes from the person concerned.

title: Outage Escalation Runbook
sections: This runbook tells the support engineer on duty what to do when customers report that the service named in the title is down or badly degraded. Start by confirming the impact: check the synthetic monitors, the error rate dashboard and the number of tickets opened in the last fifteen minutes. For this service, a severity 1 incident means {sev1_definition}. Anything smaller is a severity 2 or 3 and follows the normal queue. When in doubt, declare the higher severity; downgrading later costs nothing, while a late page costs customer trust and often breaks contractual response times.

Once severity 1 is declared, page the on-call engineer through the paging tool. The engineer must acknowledge within {ack_minutes} minutes. If there is no acknowledgement, the page escalates automatically to the secondary, and the support engineer should also phone the primary on-call lead for this service, {person}, on {phone}. Open the incident bridge in {bridge_channel} and post the incident ID, the start time, the monitors that fired and three representative ticket numbers. Keep customer details out of the bridge; link to tickets instead of pasting their content, because bridge logs are shared widely.

Customers must hear from us quickly, even before the cause is known. Publish a first status page notice within {status_page_minutes} minutes of declaring severity 1, using the investigating template, and link it in every new ticket about the outage. After that, update the status page every {update_interval}, even if the only news is that work continues. Support agents should tag all related tickets with the incident ID so they can be answered in bulk when the incident is resolved. Do not give customers an estimated time of recovery unless the incident commander has approved one in the bridge.

Mitigation decisions belong to the incident commander, who is the on-call engineer unless someone more senior takes over explicitly in the bridge. For this service, {rollback_authority} If the incident lasts more than one hour, or affects data integrity, escalate to the engineering duty manager, {person_2} ({phone_2}), who decides whether to inform executives and key accounts. Support does not contact key accounts directly during an incident; account managers do that with wording approved in the bridge. Keep a running timeline in the bridge with the time of each action, because it becomes the backbone of the review.

When monitors have been green for thirty minutes, the incident commander declares the incident resolved. Support then publishes the resolved notice, replies to tagged tickets with the approved summary, and closes them after the customer confirms. A written review is due within {postmortem_days} business days and must include the timeline, the customer impact in numbers, the root cause and follow-up actions with owners. Customers on contracts with service credits can request them based on the review's impact numbers; route those requests to billing, not to engineering. The support engineer on duty adds a short note on what slowed detection or communication.

slots.sev1_definition: more than 5 percent of payment requests failing for five minutes, or any duplicate charges

title: Mobile App Sync Troubleshooting
sections: This article helps agents fix problems where changes made on a phone or tablet do not appear on the web, or the other way round. The app syncs automatically every {sync_interval} while it is open and connected, and immediately after the user saves a record. Users can force a sync by pulling down on the record list. Before troubleshooting, confirm the app version from Settings, About, and check that the device runs at least {min_os}; older systems still open the app but sync is disabled and a banner explains why. Check the status page as well, since a backend incident looks exactly like a device problem.

Records created or edited without a connection are stored on the device and sent when the connection returns. The app can hold up to {offline_limit} of offline changes; past that point it stops accepting new edits and asks the user to reconnect. Offline changes are lost if the app is deleted or the user signs out before syncing, and the sign-out screen warns about this with the number of pending changes. Agents should always ask how many pending changes the sync indicator shows before suggesting a reinstall, because a reinstall at that point destroys the user's unsent work.

When the same record was changed on two devices before either synced, the app resolves the conflict as follows: {conflict_rule} The version that was not kept is saved in the record history for thirty days, so it can be restored by the user or an admin from the web app. Conflicts are the most common cause of reports that the app lost changes. Show the user where record history is before escalating, and ask them to avoid editing the same record on two devices at once. Admins can also export the history of a single record for review.

Photos and file attachments sync separately from record data, and only over Wi-Fi unless the user enables mobile data uploads. Each attachment can be up to {max_attachment_mb} MB; larger files stay on the device with a warning icon. If sync stops when the app is in the background, check the operating system setting: {background_setting} Battery saver modes on many devices pause background sync completely, which users rarely realise. Ask the user to keep the app open on Wi-Fi for a few minutes, which usually clears a backlog of attachments without any further action.

If the steps above do not help, collect the sync log and escalate to the mobile team. To get it, {log_steps} The log contains record IDs and timestamps but no record content, so it can be attached to the ticket safely. Escalations should include the app version, the device model, the operating system version, the number of pending changes and the time of the last successful sync. Mobile escalations are triaged by {person} ({email}) on the mobile support desk, who replies within one business day and may ask the user for a short screen recording.

After the cutoff, the app shows a banner on every screen asking the user to install the latest version from the store.

title: Two-Factor Authentication Recovery
sections: This article covers users who cannot complete two-factor sign-in because they lost their phone, changed number or deleted the authenticator app. Supported second factors on this edition are {second_factor_methods}. When a user turns on two-factor authentication, the product generates {backup_code_count} single use backup codes and asks the user to store them safely. A backup code works in place of the second factor once and is then spent. Users can see how many codes remain and generate a fresh set from their security settings, which invalidates the old set at once.

The fastest recovery path is an administrator reset. {admin_reset_rule} After the reset, the user signs in with their password only and is forced to enrol a new factor before reaching any data. Administrators should verify the request through a channel other than the one it arrived on, for example by calling the user on a number from the company directory, because second factor resets are a common target of social engineering. Every reset is recorded in the audit log with the administrator's name and the time of the change.

When the user is the only administrator, or the workspace has no administrator who can act, support runs a recovery check instead. The user submits a request from the sign-in page through the Lost access to my second factor link. We then ask for {verification_docs}. Once the check passes, a recovery hold of {recovery_wait_hours} hours starts, during which a notice is sent to every email address on the account. If nobody objects, the second factor is removed at the end of the hold. The hold cannot be shortened by support, whatever the urgency claimed.

Users can mark a browser as trusted at sign-in, which skips the second factor on that browser for {trusted_device_days} days. Trusted browsers are cleared when the password changes, when an administrator resets the factor and when the user signs out of all sessions. {enforcement_rule} Agents should remind users that a trusted browser is not a recovery method: if they lose their phone, they should generate new backup codes from the trusted browser right away, before the trust expires. Shared and public computers must never be marked as trusted.

Escalate to the identity assurance team when the documents do not match, when someone objects during the hold, or when the request looks like an account takeover attempt, for example a recent password reset followed by a factor reset from a new country. The team lead is {person} ({email}). Never read out backup codes, never disable two-factor authentication for a whole workspace on request, and never add a phone number to an account on the user's behalf. Record each recovery case with the verification evidence reference, but do not store copies of identity documents in the ticket.

These accounts are the recommended way to recover when every regular administrator is locked out, and their use triggers an alert to all other administrators. Break-glass sign-ins are also reported in the monthly security summary sent to the customer, so that every use can be reviewed and justified.

Schedule the restart outside business hours where possible, and warn the customer about it before running the tool.

title: Handling Shipping Delays
sections: This guide explains how to answer customers whose order has not arrived on time and what we can offer them. For this delivery service, orders placed before {order_cutoff} on a working day leave the warehouse the same day, and later orders leave the next working day. Delivery is handled by {carrier_name}, and the promised delivery time shown at checkout is {promised_window} from dispatch. Agents should always check the tracking page and the warehouse dispatch record before replying, because many late orders turn out to be waiting for stock and were never dispatched at all.

An order counts as late when it has not been delivered {late_threshold} after the end of the promised window. Before that point, reassure the customer, share the tracking link and explain any delay message from the carrier, such as a missed delivery attempt or a regional disruption. Do not open a carrier investigation before the order is late; the carrier rejects early requests and it delays the real one. If tracking shows the parcel was delivered but the customer has nothing, ask them to check with neighbours and any safe place for one day before treating it as missing.

Once an order is late, agents may offer {late_compensation}. Compensation is applied once per order, not per message, and is recorded on the order with the reason code LATE. If the customer no longer needs the item, they may cancel; if it arrives after cancellation, they can refuse it or return it free of charge using the refund policy steps. Customers who ask for compensation because of a carrier strike or extreme weather announced on our status banner are told plainly that the offer does not apply to announced disruptions, though they may still cancel.

A parcel with no tracking movement for {lost_after_days} working days is treated as lost. Open an investigation in the carrier portal with the tracking number and the declared value. Do not wait for the result before helping the customer: for items in stock, send a free replacement at once; for items out of stock, offer a full refund. Carrier investigations take up to three weeks, and if the parcel turns up afterwards it is returned to the warehouse. Customers never need to deal with the carrier themselves, and agents should not ask them to.

High value orders and repeated losses at the same address are reviewed by the logistics team before any replacement is sent. For this delivery service the review threshold is {review_threshold} of order value. The logistics contact who handles these reviews and carrier escalations is {person} ({email}), reachable on {phone} during warehouse hours. Agents must never share a carrier driver's name or phone number with a customer, and never promise a delivery slot that the carrier has not confirmed in tracking. If a customer complains about driver conduct, collect the details and forward them to the logistics contact, who raises it with the carrier.

Late compensation does not apply to these addresses unless the delay goes beyond that. Agents should check the shipping address before quoting any delivery estimate to the customer. For PO boxes, large items cannot be shipped at all, and the checkout should already have blocked the order.

Assembly is not included and cannot be added after dispatch. If the carrier misses the slot itself, the next slot is booked for free and the compensation above applies in full.

title: Warranty Claims and RMA Process
sections: This article explains how agents handle a warranty claim from the first contact until the repaired or replaced unit reaches the customer. Products covered here carry a warranty of {warranty_period} from the delivery date on the original invoice. Ask for the serial number, a description of the fault and the proof of purchase. Serial numbers are printed under the ear cushion, on the base plate or on the back panel depending on the product. Run the guided diagnostic in the support console before raising a return, because about a third of reported faults are fixed by a firmware update or a factory reset.

If the diagnostic confirms a hardware fault, raise a return merchandise authorisation in the console. The RMA number starts with {rma_prefix} followed by six digits and must be written on the outside of the package. The customer has {ship_window_days} days to send the unit; after that the RMA expires and a new one is needed. The repair centre for this product line is at {address}, and the console generates a prepaid label with that address where shipping is prepaid. Units sent without an RMA number are held for thirty days and then returned to the sender.

{shipping_cost_rule} Customers should remove personal accessories, ear tips, cables that were not in the original box and any stickers before sending, as the repair centre does not return items that were not part of the product. Pack the unit in the original box if possible, or in a sturdy box with padding; damage in transit caused by poor packing is not covered. Agents should tell the customer to keep the drop-off receipt until the repair centre confirms arrival, which normally happens within two working days of delivery to the centre.

The repair centre inspects each unit and either repairs it or replaces it with an equivalent unit, which may be refurbished. Target turnaround is {repair_turnaround} from arrival to dispatch. The replacement keeps the remaining original warranty or ninety days, whichever is longer. {advance_replacement_rule} If the inspection finds no fault, the unit is returned with a test report and the customer is not charged, but a second no-fault return within six months is charged an inspection fee. Customers can follow progress on the order page, where each RMA moves through received, inspected, repaired and dispatched.

The warranty does not cover {warranty_exclusions}. When inspection finds damage of this kind, the repair centre sends a quote for a paid repair, and the customer has fourteen days to accept it before the unit is returned unrepaired. Disputes about whether damage is excluded go to the warranty desk lead, {person} ({email}), who decides within five working days and may ask for photos. Statutory consumer rights in the customer's country apply in addition to this warranty, and agents must never tell a customer that the warranty replaces those rights.

title: Laptop Provisioning for New Hires
sections: This article describes how IT prepares a laptop for a new hire in the group named in the title, from the hiring manager's request to the first login. The hiring manager must raise the device request in the IT portal at least {request_lead_days} working days before the start date, as soon as the offer is signed. Requests arriving later are still handled, but the new hire may start on a loaner device. The request needs the start date, the role, the cost centre and whether the person needs any hardware beyond the standard kit, such as a second screen.

The standard device for this group is {standard_model}. Exceptions, for example a different model for accessibility reasons, need approval from the IT asset manager, {person} ({email}), and are usually granted within two days. Every device is enrolled in device management before it leaves IT, with full disk encryption turned on and the recovery key escrowed. The device is assigned to the new hire by name in the asset register, which is also where the serial number is recorded for insurance and for the return process when the person leaves the company.

Each laptop is shipped with {preinstalled_software}, plus the security agent, the VPN client and the company browser profile, which nobody may remove. Further software is installed from the self-service software center after the first login. {admin_rights_rule} Licences for paid tools are assigned to the person, not the device, and are requested by the manager in the same portal. Personal software, games and browser extensions outside the approved list are not allowed and are flagged by the security agent within a day. Operating system updates install automatically on the second Tuesday of each month.

{delivery_method} On day one, the new hire signs in with the temporary password from the welcome email, sets a new password and enrols a second factor before reaching their mailbox. IT runs a fifteen minute welcome call at 09:30 local time to check that everything works. The new hire may also order accessories, such as a monitor, keyboard, headset or docking station, from the catalogue within a budget of {accessory_budget}; items above the budget need the manager's approval. Accessories ordered in the first week usually arrive within five working days.

When the person leaves, the laptop and any accessories worth more than fifty euros must be returned within {return_days} days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid return box to the home address or collects the device at the office. Devices that are not returned are locked remotely and wiped, and their value may be deducted from the final pay where local law allows it. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to IT and to the security mailbox within twenty four hours, whatever the time of day, so that the device can be locked.

title: Troubleshooting Webhook Delivery Failures
sections: Webhooks notify a customer's server when events happen in their Orbitly workspace, such as an order being created or a payment being settled. On this tier a workspace can register up to {max_endpoints} endpoints, each subscribed to a chosen list of event types. We send each event as an HTTPS POST with a JSON body. The receiving server must answer with any 2xx status within {timeout_seconds} seconds; anything else, including a redirect, counts as a failure. Endpoints must use a public hostname with a valid TLS certificate. Self-signed certificates and plain HTTP are rejected when the endpoint is saved.

Failed deliveries are retried automatically. {retry_schedule} Each retry carries the same event ID, so receivers should store processed IDs and ignore duplicates; delivery is at least once, never exactly once, and events can arrive out of order. The delivery log in the developer dashboard shows every attempt with the status code, the response time and the first kilobyte of the response body, which is usually enough to see whether the customer's firewall, their framework or their own code rejected the call. Delivery logs are kept for thirty days and can be filtered by event type.

Every request is signed so the receiver can check that it came from us. The signature is sent in the {signature_header} header and is an HMAC SHA-256 of the timestamp and the raw request body, using the endpoint's signing secret. The most common verification bug is computing the signature over a parsed and re-serialised body rather than the raw bytes. Receivers should also reject requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes old. Signing secrets can be rotated from the endpoint page; during a rotation both secrets stay valid for twenty four hours.

{disable_rule} The workspace owners receive an email when an endpoint is disabled, and a banner appears on the developer dashboard. Once the customer has fixed their server, they re-enable the endpoint from the dashboard. Events that occurred while the endpoint was disabled are not sent automatically; they can be replayed from the event list for up to {replay_days} days, either one by one or in bulk by time range. Bulk replays are sent at a reduced pace so they do not overwhelm the receiver, and they count against the normal webhook volume.

Before escalating, ask the customer for the endpoint ID, an affected event ID and the time range. Check the delivery log for the status code pattern: timeouts point to slow processing on their side, so they should acknowledge first and process asynchronously; 401 or 403 responses usually mean a signature or firewall problem; connection errors suggest DNS or certificate issues. If the log shows no attempts at all, escalate to the integrations team through {person} ({email}), as this may be a fault on our side. Customers who need our sending IP ranges for an allowlist can find them in the developer documentation.

Agents should check which version an endpoint uses before discussing signature errors with the customer, since the rules differ.

title: Changing Subscription Plans: Upgrades and Downgrades
sections: This article explains how a customer moves between plans and what changes on their bill. Plan changes are made from Billing, Plan, by {who_can_change}. Upgrades take effect immediately: new features, limits and support levels are available as soon as the payment is confirmed. {upgrade_billing_rule} Customers who are unsure which plan fits can start a fourteen day trial of the higher plan from the same page without changing their bill, and the trial ends automatically if they do nothing. Only one trial per plan is allowed for each account, and agents cannot reset it.

Downgrades work differently. {downgrade_timing} Until then the customer keeps every feature of the current plan. When the downgrade happens, features that the lower plan lacks are switched off, but the data they created is kept read-only, so nothing is lost if the customer upgrades again later. Agents should list the features the customer will lose before confirming, using the plan comparison table, because surprises at downgrade time cause most complaints and chargebacks in this area. A scheduled downgrade can be cancelled at any time before it takes effect.

{downgrade_refund} Credits are not paid out as cash and expire if the subscription is cancelled. Customers who downgrade because of a service problem, for example after an outage, should be routed to the billing disputes process instead, because a goodwill credit may suit them better than a downgrade. Tax is recalculated on the new plan price, so customers in countries with VAT will see the tax line change too. Invoices issued before the change are never reissued. If the customer pays by bank transfer, any credit appears on the next invoice as a separate line.

Each plan has a minimum number of paid seats. For this subscription the minimum is {seat_minimum}. Removing seats follows the same timing as a downgrade, while adding seats is billed at once on a pro rata basis. If the customer's usage is above the limits of the lower plan when the downgrade runs, {over_limit_rule} Agents can see current usage against each plan's limits on the account summary and should check it before confirming any downgrade. Storage, members and automation runs are the limits that most often block a downgrade in practice.

Some changes need a person rather than the billing page: switching the billing currency, moving between monthly and annual billing in the middle of a term, merging two subscriptions, or changing the legal entity on invoices. Send these to the subscriptions team. The contact for plan change exceptions is {person} ({email}). Customers who want to leave entirely should follow the cancellation and account deletion articles; a downgrade to the lowest plan is often a better offer for customers who are leaving because of price, and agents may suggest it once, but not more than once.

variants.extra_section: Usage contract addendum: customers who exceed their committed spend by more than {overage_review_percent} percent for three months in a row are contacted by their account manager with an offer for the next tier, which usually costs less than paying overage. Agents should mention this when a customer complains about overage charges. Overage charges already invoiced are not reduced retroactively when the customer accepts such an offer for the following tier.
